defects.severity: high (read through NULL from C-valid state; the pinned authority has the same fault and it is not reproduced)
defects.description: TS_REQ_to_TS_VERIFY_CTX read ASN1_STRING_length(msg) and, when positive, passed ASN1_STRING_get0_data(msg) straight to memcpy. An ASN1_STRING with length 5 and data NULL is constructible through the exported ASN1_STRING_set0 on the object TS_MSG_IMPRINT_get_msg returns, so the copy read through NULL. The authority does the same (ts_verify_ctx.c:170).
defects.fix: Capture the data pointer once and take the existing err: arm when it is NULL; valid strings are byte-for-byte unchanged. Control: ts::ts_verify_ctx::tests::req_to_ctx_refuses_positive_length_with_null_data.
defects.divergence: Deliberate: an inconsistent (positive length, NULL data) imprint is refused instead of faulting.

defects.severity: high (data race and aliasing UB reachable from concurrent RAND_bytes / RAND_keep_random_devices_open; safe pub(crate) fns and a safe exported wrapper performed the raw access)
defects.class: unsynchronised static mut shared state (AGENTS.md sections 2, 7 and 21.3)
defects.description: RANDOM_DEVICES, KEEP_RANDOM_DEVICES_OPEN, SHM_ADDR and SEEDED were static mut. Every seeding call took &mut *addr_of_mut!(RANDOM_DEVICES) and the scalars were read/written directly, so two threads in the entropy path (or a concurrent RAND_keep_random_devices_open) minted conflicting references or raced a non-atomic write. The authority has the same unsynchronised C state; Rust makes it UB regardless of caller correctness.
defects.fix: RANDOM_DEVICES is a const-initialised Mutex with poison ignored (the authority has no poison state); the three scalars are AtomicI32/AtomicPtr with Relaxed access, matching the authority's lack of ordering requirements. The cache lock spans only the check/reopen/close transition, never a caller's read. Controls: the four rand::unix::tests cases (second acquisition + device-cache reuse, kernel fill, idempotent init/keep flag, nonce data).
defects.divergence: None observable: the same transitions happen in the same order; only the storage discipline changes.

defects.severity: low (diagnostic text only; no memory-safety effect)
defects.class: authority compatibility gap (AGENTS.md section 8 compatibility axis)
defects.description: OSSL_CMP_print_errors_cb does not reproduce cmp_util.c:158-170's ERR_SYSTEM_ERROR arm: the authority formats a system error with openssl_strerror_r and always uses ERR_GET_REASON(err) for the fallback text, while this transcription always calls ERR_reason_error_string(err) and uses the unmasked error code for the fallback reason. A system error therefore prints reason(<full code>) instead of the platform text. ERR_reason_error_string returns NULL for system errors, so the fallback is the arm taken.
defects.fix: Not repaired in this safety batch. The correction needs the ERR module's strerror helper exposed or the arm duplicated here; recorded for a compatibility sweep rather than silently changed.

defects.severity: low (authority-parity NULL argument; requires a hand-built CONF_VALUE with both members NULL)
defects.class: NULL C-string argument to BIO_puts (AGENTS.md sections 17 and 21.1)
defects.description: X509V3_EXT_val_prn calls BIO_puts(out, value) when name is NULL and BIO_puts(out, name) when value is NULL. A CONF_VALUE with both members NULL, pushable through the exported stack API, therefore passes NULL to BIO_puts, which would length-scan it. The pinned authority and OpenSSL 4.0.2 have the identical arm; the constructor paths this crate lands never produce such an entry.
defects.fix: Not repaired: recording it preserves authority parity for every constructed path. A later hardening batch should add the both-NULL skip together with the other C-string print arms so the divergence is consistent.
defects.divergence: Pre-existing authority UB, recorded; not introduced by the conversion.

defects.severity: low (authority-parity NULL argument; requires an ASN1_UTF8STRING with positive length and NULL data)
defects.class: format directive over a positive-length/NULL-data string (AGENTS.md sections 17 and 21.1)
defects.description: snprint_PKIStatusInfo_parts passes ASN1_STRING_get0_data(text) with ASN1_STRING_length(text) as the precision. An element with positive length and NULL data (constructible through ASN1_STRING_set0) makes the %.*s arm scan a NULL pointer. cmp_status.c:205-210 has the same arm.
defects.fix: Not repaired: the same both-inconsistent-object class as M29-D4; recorded for the same consistent hardening batch.
defects.divergence: Pre-existing authority UB, recorded; not introduced by the conversion.
